title: Herald endorsement: U.S. House District 20 Democratic primary | Opinion - NewsBreak
text:
By the Miami Herald Editorial Board ,
8 hours ago U.S. House District 20 Democratic candidates Luther “Uncle Luke” Campbell, Elijah Manley, Debbie Wasserman Schultz, Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick and Dale Holness. Provided The Aug. 18 Democratic primary for U.S. House District 20 is highly anticipated and filled with controversy.
The Broward County district was represented by former U.S. Rep. Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick, who resigned in April just minutes before she could face sanctions or even possible expulsion from Congress. She’s currently facing federal charges of stealing $5 million in disaster funds resulting from the overpayment of pandemic relief dollars to her healthcare company. She’s pleaded not guilty and denies any wrongdoing, and she’s running to regain her seat. That’s a mistake — if she’s found guilty her constituents will be deprived of representation again.
That leaves voters with four other choices: U.S. Rep. Debbie Wasserman Schultz, former Broward County Mayor Dale Holness, middle-school substitute teacher Elijah Manley and Luther Campbell, best known as “Uncle Luke,” a former rapper with the group 2 Live Crew.
Our choice is Wasserman Schultz, 59, a 21-year member of Congress. That was not an easy choice.
Other Democrats were right to criticize Wasserman Schultz, who’s white, for running in predominantly Black District 20 after Florida Republicans redrew her neighboring district to lean red. While we believe representation matters in Congress, so does the ability to deliver. Wasserman Schultz, who sits on the powerful House Appropriations Committee, is best positioned to bring results to a district with high rates of poverty. None of the other candidates matched her policy knowledge and expertise.
Among the achievements Wasserman Schultz cited: securing federal dollars for projects such as Port Everglades and Everglades restoration, voting to pass the Affordable Care Act in 2010 — “the most consequential piece of legislation that I have been a part of,” she said — and sponsoring the 2007 Virginia Grand Baker Pool and Spa Safety Act that required every public pool in the country to switch to safe drain covers to prevent deaths by suction drain entrapment. She also created in 2021 the Alcee L. Hastings Program for Advanced Cancer Screening in Underserved Communities, named after the late congressman who once represented the district.
All candidates agreed that the lack of affordable housing is a big issue in District 20. Wasserman Schultz said House Democrats have proposed 14 different bills to address the problem. She wants to remove red tape to allow federal housing vouchers to pay for security deposits on rentals. She also believes there’s an opportunity to use empty lots across Broward County to build homes.
She said ICE — U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement — needs “dramatic reform,” including the mandatory use of body cameras. “They are profiling people based on the color of their skin, the tenor of their accent or the language they’re speaking,” she said of ICE agents.
In April, she voted for a House measure to extend Temporary Protected Status for Haitians that’s now stuck in the U.S. Senate. She said she plans to file legislation to ensure that the Department of Homeland Security coordinates with the Department of State to assess whether the conditions in a country have improved before revoking its TPS designation.
The other candidates who attended a Herald Editorial Board interview said they also oppose the Trump administration’s revocation of Haiti’s TPS designation. Campbell was the only Democrat absent.
Manley, 27, has an inspiring story. He was homeless as a child, an experience he said “transformed my life, and it made me start to question our political system and why we have a political system that works for the billionaire class... but not for regular working people.” At 19, Manley ran for the Broward County School Board, and we encourage him to stay involved in politics. Unlike Wasserman Schultz, Manley would cut off all U.S. funding for Israel, though he supports the country’s right to exist.
Holness, 59, ran for the seat in 2021 and lost to Cherfilus-McCormick by only five votes. He said he’s running again to continue the work he started as a local elected official. He would like to repeal the cuts to food stamps Congress enacted last year and wants to reinstate subsidies under the Affordable Care Act.
The candidates agree on many issues, but one of them is in a better position to execute a vision for the district.
The Herald endorses DEBBIE WASSERMAN SCHULTZ in the U.S. House District 20 Democratic primary.
